newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends down, Brent soft as profits taken.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends down, Brent soft as profits taken.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed over $3 a tonne weaker on Thursday and Brent was also languishing late afternoon as profit-taking trimmed recent sharp gains fuelled by Middle East tension and low distillate stocks, dealers said.
Oct gas oil ended at $215.25 a tonne, down $3.25. Nov Brent shed 32 cents to $21.99 a barrel by 1630 GMT.
Dealers said gas oil and Brent fell in fairly light volume on profit-taking in the absence of fresh supportive news, although the outlook was still positive.
"Fundamentals are supportive and momentum is still positive," said a broker.
With heating oil and diesel stocks running well below year-ago levels on both sides of the Atlantic and winter approaching, traders expect the market to remain firm in the longer term.
Technical support on Oct gas oil held at around $215 a tonne but with no fresh news to stir buying interest, resistance at $219.50 -- the high for the day -- was equally impenetrable, brokers said.
Sharp losses on U.S. products combined with weaker gas oil prices to push Brent lower. The November Brent-gas oil crack spread eased 12 cents to $5.93 a barrel by the close.

News that the United States moved a second aircraft carrier into the Gulf and flew more troops to Kuwait on Thursday in a military buildup aimed at deterring any threat from Iraq caused few ripples in the market.

Recent tension between the U.S. and Iraq -- which helped push Brent to a post-Gulf War high of $24.39 a barrel last week -- appeared to be easing but the possibility of military action, and the underlying demand/supply balance would deter aggressive selling, dealers said.
